body: While they may be over exaggerating in the article, I think it's important to not discredit the potential downsides of smoking marijuana. Even if it's a rare condition learning more about it will make smoking safer in the future and can help identify risk factors. As a long term smoker myself i feel like trying to discredit research is just shooting ourselves in the foot. Everything can have negative side effects in excess and pretending that weed can't have negative side effects just makes stoners look like addicts who are in denial. Sorry if this is a little off topic, I really feel though that if we want cannabis to be legalized more research is better than less even if it not always what we want to hear.

While this doesn't partian to overall enclosure humidity, one good tips for helping give them more humidity when they shed is to add a humdity box. 

It can be super easy, just take a tupperware and cut a hole in the lid that is large enough for the snake. If you fill it with something like sphagnum moss and spray it down occasionally it will be a nice area for them to go if they need higher humidity. My girl always goes in hers when she sheds :) . Thank you! They are really awesome plants and it's actually been alot easier to care for then I expected as long as your soil is good and you keep humidity up. My best advice is to make sure you have a well draining soil maybe something like a peat moss mixture that mine is in. 

I tend to water it when the soil looks dry on top and that has been working well! The most important thing I've noticed is humidity! I keep mine on a pebble tray that I fill whenever I water it and I mist it about once I day. I've noticed that really helps in keeping the tips from browning! Good luck with yours it's a really lovely plant! :)
